= JavaScript grammar patch provenance

Upstream: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-javascript v0.25.0,
commit `44c892e0be055ac465d5eeddae6d3e194424e7de`.
The upstream MIT licence and Rust bindings are preserved. Queries are copied
from that revision, including the parameter-highlight query required by the manifest.

The JSX grammar correction: admit the existing reserved keyword terminals as
identifier aliases inside `_jsx_identifier`, including nested member names. JSX names do not carry
JavaScript's reserved-word exclusion. This admits SVG's `in`, keyword-named
attributes and namespaces without relaxing keywords in JavaScript statements
or attribute-value expressions. The current grammar, including modern
`using` declarations, remains in use; there is no grammar downgrade or TSX
fallback and no source rewriting.

The second patch also removes `export` from the upstream contextual-identifier
alternative, which incorrectly admitted it in JavaScript expressions. Property
names and export declarations remain valid. In the external scanner, CR joins
LF, U+2028 and U+2029 as a line terminator, including comments; `in` and
`instanceof` distinguish identifiers using the grammar's continuation boundary
instead of a locale-dependent alphabetic-only test.

Generated with the official tree-sitter CLI 0.27.0, native QuickJS runtime,
ABI 15: `tree-sitter generate --js-runtime native --abi 15`.
Append one final LF to `src/grammar.json` and `src/node-types.json`, which
the pinned generator omits, to meet the repository's JSON file-boundary policy.
This does not change their JSON values and is included in CI regeneration.
The official Linux x64 generator archive's verified SHA-256 is
`20a1f39ec1c45f2211492dcb8881c802b643b554bb196869a29ac3778277fa77`.
Generated parser sources are committed so consumers need no generator,
JavaScript runtime or network access to build this dependency.

The patched grammar passed the upstream `tree-sitter test` command, which
reported 116 parses and zero failures. PONS adds keyword-attribute, modern
using-declaration, malformed-JSX and reserved-keyword rejection controls.
The exact Echo warrant-debugger source is a separate executed reproducer.

This locally patched source is a direct path dependency of `pons-core`.
Registry publication of `pons-core` is disabled until the patched grammar
has a distributable package; downstream Git/path consumers retain it.
The parser receipt identifies it as `0.25.0+jsx-keywords.3`. The generated
source, patch, upstream revision and generator identity travel together;
neither a crates.io checksum nor an unmodified-upstream claim is invented.

`scripts/check-grammar-generation.sh` verifies the generator archive and
regenerates all committed generated files in Linux CI, comparing their bytes
with the shipped files. The three standard JSON metadata files are explicitly
recorded as non-JCS in `ci/json-ratchet.kyaml`; I-JSON validity remains enforced.

Revision 3 makes the identifier-continuation whitespace set explicit and
independent of the C locale. AST controls check that multiline comments before
calls, members and addition preserve one expression, including U+2028/U+2029.
The upstream 116-parse corpus remains unchanged and passes.
